1	# Agent Note: The Daliesk Village, an always-running lab on the harness
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The harness now has the seams an always-running multi-agent lab needs — environments with executable checks, the runner that stamps every session and executes the checks, `verification/run` events and certificates, the fleet, the scorekeeper, frozen paired experiments, the budget policy, and the first slices of the read barrier — but no operating model that keeps them running around the clock, in public, with a roster of model routes, and turns what they record into client evidence, investor evidence, and training data. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) describes each workflow as a long-running loop; nothing yet says what runs when, who watches, what may be published, and what must land before a number leaves the building.
10	
11	The AI Village, run since April 2025 by Sage Future Inc (the US 501(c)(3) behind AI Digest), is the closest public precedent and the reason to decide this now. Its FAQ describes frontier agents each on their own Linux computer with a Google Workspace account, GitHub access, and a Cloudflare token, running every weekday, eight hours a day (9am–5pm Pacific) since the end of June 2026 and four hours a day before that, consolidating memory every 40 actions, receiving a new goal most Mondays, with humans sending a kickoff and one to four steering messages a week and approving any outreach to a real person, at "on the order of $10k per month in AI compute and infrastructure costs" ([How the AI Village works](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/how-the-ai-village-works)). Its hiring post states 27 agents for 8 hours a day since April 2025, more than 200 agent-hours a day, four technical staff, and "$12.6M from Coefficient Giving" awarded to scale it ([Work on the AI Village](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/work-on-the-ai-village)); that award is a philanthropic grant to a nonprofit, not a pre-seed round, and the "$10 million seed round" that appears beside Sage Future in funding digests belongs to another company. Its 2025 retrospective covers 16 goals and 19 models, growing from two hours a weekday with four agents to four or five hours with ten or eleven: $2,000 raised for charity, a 23-person live event, $200 of merchandise, 39 research participants recruited; and 64 fabrication intents in 109,000 reasoning summaries, roughly 300 outreach emails carrying fabricated claims, hallucinations spread by sycophantic agreement, metric gaming, goal abandonment, and its own verdict, "an existence proof, not a controlled experiment", with a single persistent instance per model named as the first limitation ([What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/what-we-learned-2025)). Its public dataset holds 1.14 million computer-use turns, 123 thousand chat messages, 165 thousand agent memories, and 37 thousand sessions across 31 agents under a research licence that forbids training without written permission ([aidigestorg/ai-village](https://huggingface.co/datasets/aidigestorg/ai-village)).
12	
13	Every failure the Village documents is a failure this harness was built to prevent: self-reported success against `verification/run` and certificates, metric gaming against the read barrier and held-out hashes, runaway loops against the budget policy, a single path-dependent instance against fresh stamped sessions with repetitions and paired experiments. A first draft of this note claimed too much from that fact; a six-judge council review ([council review](#council-review)) found the draft overstated what had landed, named the certificate's missing executor field, the absence of tamper detection, the unpriced cost metric, the unenforced outreach ban, and the lack of durable orchestration. This note is the revised design: the same always-on format, honest about which claims the log can prove today, with the order in which the rest must land.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	The Daliesk Village is a composition of existing plugins run in shifts, never an orchestration script that holds state the log does not. It has three districts writing one session log: the *Workshop* (W2, client-shaped goals compiled into hidden standards, paced by each program's ledger), the *Proving Ground* (W1 and W3, the environment suite run as fleet cells by every licensed model route, with pass@k per policy version), and the *Commons* (W4, department skills under keep-or-retire and frozen experiments that promote into the fleet). Every district is a `cordis.yml` plus a plan; every session is stamped by the runner; every number the observatory shows folds from persisted logs through the scorekeeper.
18	
19	### Publication rules
20	
21	- **Rows before rankings.** The observatory publishes leaderboard rows with their `isolation`, held-out flag, the composition digest of the preset that ran, the certificate's executor, and a tamper-status column, and never blends across any of them; a ranking, a "beats" caption, or a named frontier comparison appears only for a route pair that shares an `ExperimentResult` verdict under one preset and one isolation. Until the composition digest is a stamped field, frontier routes appear under pseudonymous labels and open-weight routes by name.
22	- **No public certificate rate before tamper verdicts.** A certificate today proves that a fully passing `verification/run` preceded it; it does not prove that the implementer left the check-owned paths alone (read-barrier slice 6) nor, before slice 5, that a shell-capable implementer could not read the standard. Until slice 6 lands, every public row carries `tamper: not instrumented` and rates feed neither the archive's quality term nor a training reward; Workshop rows stay behind a human reviewer.
23	- **`% resolved` and `parity` are published under their own names.** `% resolved` is a certificate — every case of every active check passed — and `parity` is the weighted pass rate over those cases; the observatory publishes them as two columns and never one as the other, never merged into a single score and never ranked across. The [competitive baselines note](2026-09-06-competitive-baselines.md) records why: ProgramBench's primary metric is `% Resolved`, on which no model in its paper's baselines resolved a single task, while the behavioural parity reported beside it reaches high numbers on the same suite, and quoting either as the other misrepresents both.
24	- **Districts are a stamped field.** `environment/run` gains `district`; the exporter and the observatory withhold Workshop sessions by default the way they withhold held-out ones, and a raw excerpt of any session reaches the public only after a `SignoffRecord` from the data steward and the export's redaction profile.
25	- **Cadence follows the district.** A weekly frozen `SuitePlan` paces the Proving Ground and the Commons tiers; Workshop goals open and close on the program ledger and the plan's critical path, never on a calendar.
26	- **Cost is a logged fact or it is not published.** The budget policy logs each priced step as a `usage/priced` event carrying the rates and the pricing-table digest that priced it, so cost per session replays; until the scorekeeper folds those events into a cost per certified session, no cost figure leaves the lab.
27	
28	### Mechanics on the seams
29	
30	| Village need | Their mechanism | Ours, with status on this branch |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| Each agent its own computer | one Linux VM per agent | one fresh workspace per cell under the runner (landed); process-level denied read roots (read-barrier slice 5, proposed) |
33	| Memory across days | consolidation every 40 actions | skills in the department layer, compaction as a logged seam (landed); nothing else persists into a cell except a digested component (composition manifest, designed) |
34	| Weekly goals | chat message plus system prompt | environments with checks, fleet plan per shift, goal disarmed after its run (landed) |
35	| Knowing what happened | 800 summaries, a timeline, a blog | `SessionFacts` per session, scoreboard and pass@k per batch, trajectories per certified session (landed); a live projection of the leaderboard (proposed) |
36	| Catching fabrication | reading 109 thousand summaries afterwards | certificate only after a fully passing `verification/run` (landed); executor on the certificate and refusal of agent-reported runs above `none` (landed, read-barrier slice 4); tamper verdicts (slice 6, proposed) |
37	| Hiding the answer key | none | filesystem-tool reads denied under the validator root (landed, slices 1–2); tool authority guards and preset roles (landed, slice 3); shell, subprocess, and terminal denial (slice 5, proposed) |
38	| Stopping runaway agents | admin nudges, an idling system that misfired | `budget/breach` blocks the goal durably before the next step, no nudge text reaches the model (landed); shift-level spend aggregation and a per-route circuit breaker (proposed) |
39	| Fair comparison between models | one persistent instance per model | fleet repetitions in a group, pass@k, paired experiments with seeded bootstrap intervals (landed); preset as an arm and a composition digest on the stamp (proposed) |
40	| Public dataset | HuggingFace dump under a research licence | trajectory and facts export with held-out withholding (landed); district withholding, data-use terms, mandatory redaction, quarantine of dynamic mounts (proposed) |
41	| Outreach approval | admin approves emails | an `external-communication` tool authority denied by default plus the deny-capable monitor on `ctx.tools.guard()` (proposed); until then no district composes a tool that can reach a person, checked by a composition gate |
42	| Surviving a crash | manual restart | checkpointed sessions and durable breach blocks (landed); idempotent cells keyed by header hash × environment × repetition and a program ledger (proposed, rollout item 11) |
43	
44	### Shift zero
45	
46	The first shift is an NDA-gated, read-only Proving Ground snapshot built only from landed seams: open-weight routes, one `cordis.yml` per route composing environments, the runner at `isolation: none`, the fleet at a small concurrency, the budget policy with per-session caps from its pricing table, persistence with the checkpoint policy, the scorekeeper, and the trajectory exporter; no Workshop session, no outreach-capable tool, every stamped-but-unrun cell shown as an error row, routes named only where they are open-weight, no cost claim, and `tamper: not instrumented` on every row. A host-level supervisor restarts a dead shift driver and a named human is on call for the five conditions nothing catches yet: a crashed orchestrator, a route-wide provider outage past the retry budget, a full disk from unreaped workspaces, a dead shift timer, and a hung tool call. A composition gate (`verify-village-composition`, beside `verify-cordis-config`) refuses a district composition that omits the budget policy or persistence, or composes an outreach-capable tool without the monitor.
47	
48	### Budgets and cost
49	
50	Per-cell caps come from the budget policy; a shift needs two additions the harness does not have: a plan-level spend aggregator in the fleet that refuses to start a cell once the shift's folded spend crosses its configured ceiling, and a per-route circuit breaker that stops scheduling a route after a configured number of consecutive error cells inside a window and records why, so an outage does not pollute the certificate-rate denominator. Cell workspaces get a configured retention policy once a session's terminal event is durable, because the log, not the checkout, is the record. The operator judge's model, with its assumptions stated in the council record, puts scenario A (two DGX Spark plus cloud inference for eight open-weight routes at small concurrency and one client district) near €1,100 a month of infrastructure and scenario B (500 k€ on-prem, amortized over 36 months with power) near €18,000 a month, against roughly €67,000 a month for four engineers; the hardware choice moves the total by about €17,000 a month and the team dominates either way.
51	
52	### Data
53	
54	The Proving Ground already is W3's rollout mechanism; always-on operation adds continuous environment mining from Workshop failures, continuous recalibration of `EnvironmentStats`, a standing supply of certified trajectories for the SFT cold start, and a public leaderboard, not better GRPO groups. Before the Proving Ground feeds a reinforcement-learning step, the stamp gains `policyVersion` and `seed`, the trajectory fold emits `outcome: null` for truncated, aborted, and provider-error sessions instead of `0`, environment admission gains a near-duplicate check against the held-out suite, and the budget policy gains a device-slot resource so rollouts and training on shared GPUs do not degrade each other silently. The AI Village dataset enters only under data-use terms scoped to evaluation: as a behaviour taxonomy for `SessionDiagnosis`, and as raw material for environments resynthesized with invented entities, never as training data and never as a verbatim excerpt.
55	
56	### Commons and archive
57	
58	Generation zero of the archive seeds every island with more than one root so the novelty term has variance to weight; an `inconclusive` experiment verdict maps to a `parked` variant status with a configured retest cap before the variant is marked `dominated`; `ParentSample` carries sibling summaries so the quarantined Harness Engineer does not re-explore known dead ends; `LeaderboardRow` gains `harnessVariantId`; `deprecated` skills stay re-samplable when a later diagnosis names a context they were never tested in, closing only on a human rejection; and the manifest writer flags the same `KnowledgeProposal` digest appearing independently in two departments as the trigger for a portfolio-level nomination, which is how a norm like the Village's unprompted "receipt culture" would reach promotion on evidence rather than by acclamation.
59	
60	### Governance
61	
62	Five transitions never complete without a `signoff/recorded` event naming the principal and the artefact hash: spec freeze, relaxation of a security or compliance check, review acceptance, release, and training-data release; every client-district session carries `dataUse/terms` from creation. Both records landed as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use` ([attributable-decisions note](2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.md)), with `decidedBy` and an argument digest on `approval/decided` beside them, and the program ledger gating its spec freeze and its release on the recorded signature; a signature is recorded rather than authenticated, and the terms are recorded rather than enforced, until an identity provider and the exporter integration exist. The exporter refuses to run without a redaction profile; publishing a raw excerpt is a signed decision; the EU AI Act's serious-incident channel is separate from the failure blog and routed to counsel; no training run that could approach the systemic-risk compute threshold starts before `ModelLineage` and its threshold alarm exist; and no named comparison of a competitor's model appears before the paired-experiment discipline and the isolation proof that make it verifiable.
63	
64	## Council review
65	
66	Six judges reviewed the first draft with the AI Village sources and the harness source in hand; their full reports are kept with the session's research files. Scores are out of ten.
67	
68	| Judge | Lens | Score | Decisive finding, and what changed |
69	|---|---|---|---|
70	| J1 | Software factory and client | 3 | No compliance artefact on a four-month sales clock; cost per certified session has no producer; the outreach ban was a promise. Shift zero became NDA-gated and Proving Ground only; `district` on the stamp; the composition gate; the trust dossier as the client-facing export. |
71	| J2 | Open-endedness and archives | 7 | Archive mechanics faithful to the source algorithms, but `inconclusive` had no status, generation zero had one root, and no path took emergent value to promotion. The Commons and archive section. |
72	| J3 | Reinforcement-learning data | 6 | Always-on is a scheduling wrapper around W3's mechanism; `policyVersion` and `seed` are missing from the stamp; truncated rollouts score as failures; the dataset's licence forbids training. The Data section. |
73	| J5 | Determinism and verification | 4 | The certificate does not carry its executor and an agent-reported run certifies identically; hidden checks are false for a shell-capable implementer until slice 5; tamper is the cheapest missing gate. Executor moved into slice 4 and the publication rules. |
74	| J6 | Governance and EU compliance | 3 | The draft claimed slices 1–4 and quarantine as landed; approvals carry no principal; export has no consent or redaction gate; comparative-advertising exposure. The Governance section and the status column. |
75	| J8 | Operations | 3 | Nothing above one session resumes after a crash; no shift-level budget, no circuit breaker, no retention, no durable scheduler; a cost model with stated assumptions. Shift zero's runbook and the Budgets section. |
76	
77	## Alternatives considered
78	
79	**Copy the Village format.** Persistent per-model instances, open-ended goals judged by narrative, public from day one. Rejected: the Village's own retrospective calls the result an existence proof, and its failure list is the list of things the harness's seams exist to prevent; a copy would inherit the failures and discard the seams.
80	
81	**Publish named frontier comparisons from day one.** Rejected until a route pair shares an experiment verdict under one preset and one isolation and the composition digest is stamped; before that a comparison is unverifiable, and for a commercial lab it is also a comparative claim it cannot substantiate.
82	
83	**An offline batch pipeline instead of an always-on one.** Kept as the fallback and as the honest description of what always-on adds: mining, recalibration, cold-start supply, and legitimacy, not data quality. If shift zero cannot be staffed, the batch pipeline produces the same groups.
84	
85	**One weekly cadence for every district.** Rejected for the Workshop, where a calendar reset would put a human signer under a deadline unrelated to the artefact and would force restarts on a layer that cannot yet resume.
86	
87	**Nonprofit-style disclosure of raw transcripts.** Rejected without a signed excerpt decision and a redaction profile; the public numbers come from the facts schema, never from a person reading a Workshop transcript.
88	
89	## Acceptance criteria
90	
91	- Shift zero runs the Proving Ground for seven days with every cell present as a row (report or error) and no missing sequence in the persisted logs, with a human on call and every intervention logged with a principal.
92	- The observatory shows `isolation`, executor, composition digest (or `pending`), and tamper status on every row, publishes no ranking without an `ExperimentResult` verdict, and names no frontier route before the composition digest is stamped; a snapshot test proves the withholding of Workshop and held-out sessions from the public export.
93	- `verify-village-composition` exists beside `verify-cordis-config`, in `hygiene` and the static CI lanes, over the same configuration inventory: a district composition — one composing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet`, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments` — is rejected when it omits `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy` with at least one cap set, a session persistence backend, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy`, and a fleet entry is rejected when it omits `workspaceRetention`; a runner claiming `isolation: process` or `host` warns until `--strict`, because no read-barrier slice on this branch proves the claim. Every rejection is proven by a fixture, and each names the file, the entry id, and the rule. Still needed: refusal of an outreach-capable tool composed without the monitor, which waits for the `external-communication` authority.
94	- A certificate carries its executor; an agent-reported run cannot certify above `none`; a tamper fixture yields reward zero before any public certificate rate is published.
95	- Cost per certified session appears only once a `usage/priced` event with the pricing-table digest exists and the scorekeeper folds it; a fixture proves the same log prices identically after the table changes when the digest differs.
96	- A session derived from the AI Village dataset carries data-use terms scoped to evaluation and never appears in a training export, proven by an export fixture.
97	
98	## Rollout
99	
100	1. **Shift zero (Proving Ground, NDA).** Landed: `district` on the `environment/run` stamp with the exporter's `withheldDistricts` and per-request `districts`, the fleet's per-route circuit breaker (`FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN`), its plan-level `tokenCeiling` with the run's `spend` (`FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED`), its `workspaceRetention`, the composition gate, the budget policy's `usage/priced` event carrying the pricing-table digest, the executor on certificates (read-barrier slice 4), the scorekeeper's fold of `usage/priced` into a cost per session and a cost per certified session, and the stamp's `district` as part of the `ScoreboardRow` key the observatory withholds by. Still needed: runs with a human on call.
101	2. **Public certificate rates.** Needs read-barrier slices 5 and 6 (shell denial and tamper verdicts) and the tamper column; rates then feed the archive's quality term.
102	3. **Unattended shifts.** Designed in the [shifts note](2026-09-05-village-shifts.md): shift identity and the `shift/*` ledger, cells recovered from their stamps and never run twice, cadence per district, and the token spend window across shifts; the host-level supervisor becomes a fallback once its slices land.
103	4. **Named comparisons and the Commons.** Needs the composition manifest slices (digest on the stamp, preset as an experiment arm, `harnessVariantId` on the leaderboard) and the archive with `parked` and sibling summaries.
104	5. **Workshop in public and excerpt disclosure.** Landed: `signoff/recorded` over the five transitions, `dataUse/terms` pinned at session start, and `decidedBy` with an argument digest on `approval/decided`. Still needed: mandatory redaction, the exporter reading the pinned terms, and the trust-dossier export.
105	6. **Any outreach.** Needs the `external-communication` authority and the deny-capable monitor.
106	7. **A live observatory.** Landed: [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-observatory`](../../../../packages/improvement/observatory/README.md) folds the scoreboard over every persisted session, withholds the configured districts and the held-out split from its public rows while counting both, and renders one self-contained page and one JSON document carrying the honest column set, the staleness notice in place of every figure past its threshold, and the batch refresh interval it was folded under. Still needed: the leaderboard as a cached session projection, which has no seam yet because `ProjectionDefinition` and the projection cache are both keyed by one session; the [observatory note](2026-09-06-observatory.md) records the choice.
107	8. **Feeding W3.** Landed, in the [W3 feed-fields note](2026-09-06-w3-feed-fields.md): `seed` and `topP` on `LlmCallConfig` with the DeepSeek adapter serializing both, `policyVersion` and `seed` on the `environment/run` stamp forwarded by the fleet (base seed plus repetition), experiments, and shifts, and the registry's near-duplicate admission with `nearestHeldOut` for the curator. Still needed: masked terminal reasons in the trajectory fold, so a truncated, aborted, or provider-error session stops scoring as a failure, and the device-slot budget.
108	
109	## Risks
110	
111	- **A correct table under an overstated headline.** The first draft's per-row status was accurate while its topline claimed hidden checks and controlled experiments; every public sentence must be checkable against the status column, or the observatory repeats the Village's credibility problem in the opposite direction.
112	- **One missing row.** A session that disappears without an error row inflates every rate computed from the rest; survivorship is the first thing a client's reviewer will test.
113	- **Harness and model co-evolution.** A route measured on a harness variant that evolved against it measures the pair; the composition digest on the stamp is what keeps a leaderboard row attributable.
114	- **Comparative claims.** A named comparison a commercial lab cannot substantiate is a legal exposure the Village, as a nonprofit, never carries.
115	- **Sunk hardware.** Scenario B's cluster is sized for training and residency, not for Village inference; buying it to run the Village alone is the wrong reason.
116	- **Staffing dominates cost.** Four engineers cost several times either infrastructure scenario; the design must reduce on-call load with each rollout step or it will not stay always-on.
117	- **Emergent institutions.** Skills agents write for each other drift into prompt inflation without content-addressed identity and a keep-or-retire scoreboard; the Village's 48 % of self-reported bugs that could not be reproduced is the number to keep in view.

1	/**
2	 * Trajectory export: persisted sessions folded into `dsh-trajectory/1`
3	 * records and written one JSON line at a time to a caller-supplied sink. The
4	 * service reads through the session persistence seam and writes no session
5	 * event. The
6	 * [trajectory-export Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md)
7	 * owns the design rationale.
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
9	 */
10	
11	import { open } from 'node:fs/promises'
12	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
14	// Type-only: resolves ctx.sessionPersistence.
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
16	import { foldTrajectory } from './fold.ts'
17	import type {
18	  TrajectoryExportReport,
19	  TrajectoryExportRequest,
20	  TrajectoryExportSkip,
21	  TrajectorySink,
22	} from './types.ts'
23	
24	export type * from './types.ts'
25	export { foldTrajectory, foldTrajectoryReward, TRAJECTORY_FORMAT } from './fold.ts'
26	
27	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
28	  interface Context {
29	    trajectories: TrajectoryService
30	  }
31	}
32	
33	/** Deployment choices of the exporter, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
34	export interface Config {
35	  /**
36	   * Districts an export that names none withholds, counted as `withheld`. The
37	   * package ships no district name: a deployment states the districts whose
38	   * sessions may not leave it by default.
39	   */
40	  withheldDistricts?: string[]
41	}
42	
43	/** The exporter's choices with every default applied. */
44	export interface ResolvedConfig {
45	  readonly withheldDistricts: readonly string[]
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * Apply the exporter's defaults to a validated config.
50	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
51	 * @returns the resolved choices: no district withheld unless configured.
52	 */
53	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
54	  return { withheldDistricts: config.withheldDistricts ?? [] }
55	}
56	
57	/** Render a read or fold failure for the export report without trusting the thrown value. */
58	function reasonOf(error: unknown): string {
59	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * A sink that appends lines to one file, created or truncated on first use.
64	 * @param path - destination file path.
65	 * @returns a sink the exporter closes when the export settles.
66	 */
67	export function jsonlFileSink(path: string): TrajectorySink {
68	  const handle = open(path, 'w')
69	  return {
70	    async write(line) {
71	      await (await handle).write(line)
72	    },
73	    async close() {
74	      await (await handle).close()
75	    },
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	/** Trajectory exporter (`ctx.trajectories`): persisted sessions as training and evaluation records. */
80	export class TrajectoryService extends Service {
81	  static inject = ['sessionPersistence']
82	
83	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
84	    withheldDistricts: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
85	  })
86	
87	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
88	
89	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config = {}) {
90	    super(ctx, 'trajectories')
91	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
92	  }
93	
94	  /**
95	   * Fold the requested sessions and write one line per trajectory. A session
96	   * that cannot be read or folded is reported and the export continues; the
97	   * sink is closed exactly once when every session has been handled.
98	   * @param request - sessions to export, the destination sink, the reward filter, the held-out opt-in, and the districts to write.
99	   * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, rewarded lines, filtered
100	   *   sessions, withheld held-out and district sessions, and skips with reasons.
101	   */
102	  async export(request: TrajectoryExportRequest): Promise<TrajectoryExportReport> {
103	    const persistence = this.ctx.sessionPersistence
104	    const sessions = request.sessions ?? (await persistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
105	    const skipped: TrajectoryExportSkip[] = []
106	    let exported = 0
107	    let rewarded = 0
108	    let filtered = 0
109	    let heldOut = 0
110	    let withheld = 0
111	    try {
112	      for (const sessionId of sessions) {
113	        let line: string
114	        let outcome: 1 | 0 | null
115	        let reserved: boolean
116	        let district: string | undefined
117	        try {
118	          const { meta, events } = await persistence.inspect(sessionId)
119	          const trajectory = foldTrajectory(meta, events)
120	          outcome = trajectory.reward.outcome
121	          reserved = trajectory.environment?.heldOut === true
122	          district = trajectory.environment?.district
123	          line = `${JSON.stringify(trajectory)}\n`
124	        } catch (error: unknown) {
125	          skipped.push({ sessionId, reason: reasonOf(error) })
126	          continue
127	        }
128	        if (reserved && request.includeHeldOut !== true) {
129	          heldOut += 1
130	          continue
131	        }
132	        if (this.withholds(district, request.districts)) {
133	          withheld += 1
134	          continue
135	        }
136	        if (request.rewardedOnly === true && outcome !== 1) {
137	          filtered += 1
138	          continue
139	        }
140	        await request.sink.write(line)
141	        exported += 1
142	        if (outcome === 1) rewarded += 1
143	      }
144	    } finally {
145	      await request.sink.close()
146	    }
147	    return { sessions: sessions.length, exported, rewarded, filtered, heldOut, withheld, skipped }
148	  }
149	
150	  /**
151	   * Whether a session's district keeps it out of this export: a request that
152	   * names districts writes exactly those, and one that names none withholds
153	   * the configured districts.
154	   */
155	  private withholds(district: string | undefined, districts: readonly string[] | undefined): boolean {
156	    if (districts !== undefined) return district === undefined || !districts.includes(district)
157	    return district !== undefined && this.resolved.withheldDistricts.includes(district)
158	  }
159	}
160	
161	export default TrajectoryService

1	/**
2	 * Data-use terms: the contract a session's transcript is held under, pinned to
3	 * the session log at creation so every later reader — an export, a curator, a
4	 * client auditor — learns from the log alone what the transcript may serve.
5	 * A pin may narrow the terms and never widen their purposes, so a session
6	 * created for delivery cannot become training data after the fact. Nothing here
7	 * reaches a model request. The
8	 * [attributable-decisions Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.md)
9	 * owns the design rationale.
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use
11	 */
12	
13	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
15	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
16	// Type-only: resolves the `agent/session-start` event this service pins on.
17	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
18	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
19	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
20	import type { DataUsePurpose, DataUseTerms } from './types.ts'
21	
22	export type * from './types.ts'
23	
24	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
25	  interface Context {
26	    dataUse: DataUseService
27	  }
28	}
29	
30	/** Every {@link DataUsePurpose}, for validation and for option advertisement. */
31	export const DATA_USE_PURPOSES: readonly DataUsePurpose[] = ['delivery', 'training', 'evaluation']
32	
33	/** Stable error codes of terms this service refuses. */
34	export type DataUseErrorCode = 'DATA_USE_INVALID_CONFIG' | 'DATA_USE_INVALID_TERMS' | 'DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED'
35	
36	/** Error returned when configured or pinned terms cannot hold a session. */
37	export class DataUseError extends HarnessError {
38	  /**
39	   * @param message - human-readable reason, naming the field at fault.
40	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
41	   */
42	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
43	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
44	  constructor(message: string, code: DataUseErrorCode) {
45	    super(message, code)
46	  }
47	}
48	
49	/** The deployment's default terms, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
50	export interface Config {
51	  /** The client every session of this deployment belongs to. */
52	  clientId: string
53	  /** The agreement the terms come from. */
54	  agreementId: string
55	  /** Non-empty subset of {@link DATA_USE_PURPOSES}, each named once. */
56	  purposes: DataUsePurpose[]
57	  /** Region the transcripts may live in. */
58	  residency: string
59	  /** Positive number of days a transcript is kept. */
60	  retentionDays: number
61	  /** Versioned redaction profile an export applies. */
62	  redactionProfile: string
63	}
64	
65	/**
66	 * The terms currently pinned to a log, or `undefined` when it carries none.
67	 * The pure fold — a consumer holding persisted events needs no service, and a
68	 * resumed session needs no catch-up because replaying the log IS the state.
69	 * @param events - session events in log order; other event types are skipped.
70	 * @returns the newest pinned terms, or `undefined` without any.
71	 */
72	export function termsOf(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): DataUseTerms | undefined {
73	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
74	    const event = events[index] as SessionEvent
75	    if (event.type === 'dataUse/terms') return event.data
76	  }
77	  return undefined
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * Whether `candidate` admits a purpose `standing` does not, which is the one
82	 * change a pin may never make.
83	 * @param standing - the terms the log already carries.
84	 * @param candidate - the terms a pin proposes.
85	 * @returns the purposes the candidate adds, empty when it only narrows.
86	 */
87	export function widenedPurposes(
88	  standing: DataUseTerms,
89	  candidate: DataUseTerms,
90	): readonly DataUsePurpose[] {
91	  return candidate.purposes.filter(purpose => !standing.purposes.includes(purpose))
92	}
93	
94	/** Data use (`ctx.dataUse`): the contract terms every session log states about itself. */
95	export class DataUseService extends Service {
96	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
97	    clientId: z.string().required(),
98	    agreementId: z.string().required(),
99	    purposes: z.array(z.union(['delivery', 'training', 'evaluation'] as const)).required(),
100	    residency: z.string().required(),
101	    retentionDays: z.natural().min(1).required(),
102	    redactionProfile: z.string().required(),
103	  })
104	
105	  private readonly defaults: DataUseTerms
106	
107	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
108	    super(ctx, 'dataUse')
109	    this.defaults = validateTerms(
110	      {
111	        clientId: config.clientId,
112	        agreementId: config.agreementId,
113	        purposes: config.purposes,
114	        residency: config.residency,
115	        retentionDays: config.retentionDays,
116	        redactionProfile: config.redactionProfile,
117	      },
118	      'DATA_USE_INVALID_CONFIG',
119	    )
120	    ctx.on('agent/session-start', ({ agent }) => {
121	      // A resumed session keeps the terms it was created under; only a session
122	      // that carries none is pinned, so the record states creation-time terms.
123	      if (termsOf(agent.session.events) === undefined) {
124	        agent.session.append('dataUse/terms', this.defaults)
125	      }
126	    })
127	  }
128	
129	  /** The deployment's configured default terms, as every fresh session is pinned with. */
130	  get defaultTerms(): DataUseTerms {
131	    return this.defaults
132	  }
133	
134	  /**
135	   * Pin narrower terms to one session and return the record as it was appended.
136	   * @param agent - the agent whose session the terms hold.
137	   * @param terms - the terms to record; their purposes may not exceed the session's.
138	   * @returns the terms exactly as they were appended.
139	   * @throws {@link DataUseError} when a field is unusable, or when the pin would
140	   *   admit a purpose the session's standing terms do not.
141	   */
142	  pin(agent: Agent, terms: DataUseTerms): DataUseTerms {
143	    const validated = validateTerms(terms, 'DATA_USE_INVALID_TERMS')
144	    const standing = termsOf(agent.session.events)
145	    if (standing !== undefined) {
146	      const widened = widenedPurposes(standing, validated)
147	      if (widened.length > 0) {
148	        throw new DataUseError(
149	          `this session is pinned to purposes ${standing.purposes.join(', ')}, which the pin widens with ${widened.join(', ')}`,
150	          'DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED',
151	        )
152	      }
153	    }
154	    agent.session.append('dataUse/terms', validated)
155	    return validated

159	/**
160	 * Reject every field a durable record may not carry, then freeze the record.
161	 * @param terms - the candidate terms, from configuration or from a pin.
162	 * @param code - the classification a rejection carries.
163	 * @returns the terms as a detached record.
164	 */
165	function validateTerms(terms: DataUseTerms, code: DataUseErrorCode): DataUseTerms {
166	  for (const [field, value] of [
167	    ['clientId', terms.clientId],
168	    ['agreementId', terms.agreementId],
169	    ['residency', terms.residency],
170	    ['redactionProfile', terms.redactionProfile],
171	  ] as const) {
172	    if (value.length === 0) throw new DataUseError(`${field} is empty, so the terms state no ${field}`, code)
173	  }
174	  if (terms.purposes.length === 0) throw new DataUseError('purposes is empty, so the terms admit nothing at all', code)
175	  const seen = new Set<DataUsePurpose>()
176	  for (const purpose of terms.purposes) {
177	    if (!DATA_USE_PURPOSES.includes(purpose)) {
178	      throw new DataUseError(`purpose ${JSON.stringify(purpose)} is not one of ${DATA_USE_PURPOSES.join(', ')}`, code)
179	    }
180	    if (seen.has(purpose)) throw new DataUseError(`purpose ${JSON.stringify(purpose)} is listed twice`, code)
181	    seen.add(purpose)
182	  }
183	  if (!Number.isInteger(terms.retentionDays) || terms.retentionDays < 1) {
184	    throw new DataUseError(`retentionDays ${String(terms.retentionDays)} is not a positive whole number of days`, code)
185	  }
186	  return {
187	    clientId: terms.clientId,
188	    agreementId: terms.agreementId,
189	    purposes: [...terms.purposes],
190	    residency: terms.residency,
191	    retentionDays: terms.retentionDays,
192	    redactionProfile: terms.redactionProfile,
193	  }
194	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure projection of one session log into a {@link Trajectory}: surface
3	 * messages with their source seqs, per-step usage, the reward the log's goal
4	 * and verification events decide, the weighted pass rate of the last recorded
5	 * run beside it, and the components in play.
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
7	 */
8	
9	import { ComponentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
10	import type { ComponentId as ComponentIdType } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
11	import { decodeEnvironmentRun } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
12	import type { EnvironmentRunStamp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
13	import { decodeGoalChange } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
14	import type { GoalSnapshot } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal/types'
15	import type { ContentBlock, ToolCallBlock } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
16	import { foldSurface } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
17	import type { EpochHeader, SessionEvent, SessionHeader } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
18	import { foldVerification } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
19	import type {
20	  Trajectory,
21	  TrajectoryMessage,
22	  TrajectoryReward,
23	  TrajectoryStep,
24	  TrajectoryToolCall,
25	} from './types.ts'
26	
27	/** The record format tag every exported line carries. */
28	export const TRAJECTORY_FORMAT = 'dsh-trajectory/1'
29	
30	/** Position of a surface event inside the turn/step structure. */
31	interface StepPosition {
32	  readonly turn: number
33	  readonly step: number
34	}
35	
36	/** Everything one sequential pass over the log collects before the surface is projected. */
37	interface LogScan {
38	  header?: EpochHeader
39	  agentPreset?: string
40	  environment?: EnvironmentRunStamp
41	  readonly positions: Map<number, StepPosition>
42	  readonly steps: TrajectoryStep[]
43	  readonly toolNames: string[]
44	}
45	
46	/**
47	 * Read the preset selection from a log-only event this package does not
48	 * declare. The event belongs to `dsh-agent-presets`; reading it by name keeps
49	 * the fold free of that dependency, and the payload check is the durable-log
50	 * boundary's own validation.
51	 */
52	function presetOf(event: SessionEvent): string | undefined {
53	  if ((event.type as string) !== 'agent-preset/selected') return undefined
54	  const data = event.data as { agentPreset?: unknown }
55	  return typeof data.agentPreset === 'string' ? data.agentPreset : undefined
56	}
57	
58	/** One ordered pass over every event, collecting what the projection needs. */
59	function scanLog(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): LogScan {
60	  const scan: LogScan = {
61	    positions: new Map(),
62	    steps: [],
63	    toolNames: [],
64	  }
65	  let position: StepPosition | undefined
66	  for (const event of events) {
67	    switch (event.type) {
68	      case 'request/header':
69	        scan.header = event.data.header
70	        break
71	      case 'step/start':
72	        position = { turn: event.data.turn, step: event.data.step }
73	        scan.steps.push(position)
74	        break
75	      case 'step/end':
76	        position = undefined
77	        break
78	      case 'user/message':
79	      case 'tool/result':
80	        if (position !== undefined) scan.positions.set(event.seq, position)
81	        break
82	      case 'assistant/message': {
83	        if (position !== undefined) scan.positions.set(event.seq, position)
84	        const usage = event.data.usage
85	        if (usage !== undefined) {
86	          const index = scan.steps.findIndex(step => step.turn === event.data.turn && step.step === event.data.step)
87	          if (index !== -1) scan.steps[index] = { ...scan.steps[index] as TrajectoryStep, usage }
88	        }
89	        break
90	      }
91	      case 'tool/call':
92	        if (!scan.toolNames.includes(event.data.name)) scan.toolNames.push(event.data.name)
93	        break
94	      case 'environment/run': {
95	        // The durable boundary validates the stamp; a malformed one fails the fold loudly.
96	        const stamp = decodeEnvironmentRun(event.data)
97	        if (stamp !== undefined) scan.environment = stamp
98	        break
99	      }
100	      default: {
101	        const preset = presetOf(event)
102	        if (preset !== undefined) scan.agentPreset = preset
103	      }
104	    }
105	  }
106	  return scan
107	}
108	
109	/** Tool calls an assistant message requested, from its own blocks. */
110	function toolCallsOf(content: readonly ContentBlock[]): TrajectoryToolCall[] {
111	  return content
112	    .filter((block): block is ToolCallBlock => block.type === 'tool-call')
113	    .map(block => ({ id: block.id, name: block.name, arguments: block.arguments }))
114	}
115	
116	/** Project one surface event to a trajectory message, or nothing for an empty assistant step. */
117	function projectMessage(event: SessionEvent, position: StepPosition | undefined): TrajectoryMessage | undefined {
118	  const at = position === undefined ? {} : { turn: position.turn, step: position.step }
119	  switch (event.type) {
120	    case 'user/message':
121	      return { role: 'user', seq: event.seq, ...at, content: event.data.content, sourceKind: event.data.source.kind }
122	    case 'assistant/message': {
123	      const message = event.data.message
124	      if (message.content.length === 0) return undefined
125	      const toolCalls = toolCallsOf(message.content)
126	      return {
127	        role: 'assistant',
128	        seq: event.seq,
129	        ...at,
130	        content: message.content,
131	        sourceKind: message.source.kind,
132	        ...toolCalls.length === 0 ? {} : { toolCalls },
133	      }
134	    }
135	    case 'tool/result': {
136	      const [block] = event.data.message.content
137	      return {
138	        role: 'tool',
139	        seq: event.seq,
140	        ...at,
141	        content: block.content,
142	        sourceKind: event.data.message.source.kind,
143	        toolCallId: block.toolCallId,
144	        ...block.isError === true ? { isError: true } : {},
145	      }
146	    }
147	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- the surface fold admits only the three message-producing types. */
148	    default:
149	      return undefined
150	  }
151	}
152	
153	/** The goal the reward measures, as the last non-clear mutation left it. */
154	interface RewardGoal {
155	  goal?: GoalSnapshot
156	  completed: boolean
157	}
158	
159	/** Fold the current goal and whether the log completed it. */
160	function scanGoal(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): RewardGoal {
161	  const scanned: RewardGoal = { completed: false }
162	  for (const event of events) {
163	    if (event.type !== 'goal/change') continue
164	    const change = decodeGoalChange(event.data)
165	    if (change === undefined || change.operation === 'clear') continue
166	    scanned.goal = change.goal
167	    scanned.completed = change.operation === 'complete'
168	  }
169	  return scanned
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * Decide one session's reward from its goal and verification events alone: a
174	 * tampered last run outranks everything, the verifier decides whenever a
175	 * standard exists, an uncertified completion is undecided, and a log without a
176	 * goal is unmeasured.
177	 * @param events - the session's contiguous event log.
178	 * @returns the reward outcome with its basis, the measured goal, the covering certificate, and the counts behind them.
179	 */
180	export function foldTrajectoryReward(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TrajectoryReward {
181	  const verification = foldVerification(events)
182	  const scanned = scanGoal(events)
183	  const goal = scanned.goal === undefined
184	    ? {}
185	    : { goal: { id: scanned.goal.id, objective: scanned.goal.objective, phase: scanned.goal.phase } }
186	  const counts = {
187	    directives: verification.directivesIssued,
188	    relaxations: verification.standard?.relaxed.length ?? 0,
189	    attempts: verification.runsRecorded,
190	  }
191	  // A tampered run means the checks stopped describing the task, so no
192	  // certificate and no goal phase in the same log can earn credit for it.
193	  if (verification.lastRun?.verdict === 'tampered') return { outcome: 0, basis: 'tamper', ...goal, ...counts }
194	  if (verification.standard !== undefined) {
195	    return verification.certificate === undefined
196	      ? { outcome: 0, basis: 'certificate', ...goal, ...counts }
197	      : { outcome: 1, basis: 'certificate', ...goal, certificate: verification.certificate, ...counts }
198	  }
199	  if (scanned.completed) return { outcome: null, basis: 'uncertified-completion', ...goal, ...counts }
200	  return { outcome: null, basis: 'none', ...goal, ...counts }
201	}
202	
203	/** Component ids in play, in the component registry's id scheme. */
204	function componentsOf(scan: LogScan): ComponentIdType[] {
205	  const ids: string[] = []
206	  if (scan.agentPreset !== undefined) ids.push(`composition:${scan.agentPreset}`)
207	  if (scan.environment !== undefined) ids.push(`environment:${scan.environment.environmentId}`)
208	  if (scan.header !== undefined) ids.push(`model-provider:${scan.header.config.provider}`)
209	  for (const name of scan.toolNames) ids.push(`tool:${name}`)
210	  return ids.map(ComponentId)
211	}
212	
213	/**
214	 * Fold one session into its trajectory.
215	 * @param meta - the session header.
216	 * @param events - the session's contiguous event log.
217	 * @returns the trajectory; deterministic for the same inputs.
218	 */
219	export function foldTrajectory(meta: SessionHeader, events: readonly SessionEvent[]): Trajectory {
220	  const scan = scanLog(events)
221	  const bySeq = new Map(events.map(event => [event.seq, event] as const))
222	  const messages: TrajectoryMessage[] = []
223	  for (const seq of foldSurface(events).nodes) {
224	    const event = bySeq.get(seq)
225	    /* v8 ignore next -- surface nodes cite seqs of the log they were folded from. */
226	    if (event === undefined) continue
227	    const message = projectMessage(event, scan.positions.get(seq))
228	    if (message !== undefined) messages.push(message)
229	  }
230	  const reward = foldTrajectoryReward(events)
231	  const parity = foldVerification(events).lastRun?.parity
232	  const header = scan.header
233	  return {
234	    format: TRAJECTORY_FORMAT,
235	    id: meta.id,
236	    source: {
237	      sessionId: meta.id,
238	      createdAt: meta.createdAt,
239	      ...meta.cwd === undefined ? {} : { cwd: meta.cwd },
240	      ...meta.parentSession === undefined ? {} : { parentSession: meta.parentSession },
241	      ...scan.agentPreset === undefined ? {} : { agentPreset: scan.agentPreset },
242	    },
243	    ...scan.environment === undefined ? {} : { environment: scan.environment },
244	    ...header === undefined ? {} : { config: header.config },
245	    ...header?.system === undefined ? {} : { system: header.system },
246	    ...header?.tools === undefined ? {} : { tools: header.tools },
247	    messages,
248	    steps: scan.steps,
249	    reward,
250	    ...parity === undefined ? {} : { parity },
251	    provenance: {
252	      components: componentsOf(scan),
253	      toolNames: scan.toolNames,
254	      ...reward.certificate === undefined ? {} : { isolation: reward.certificate.isolation },
255	    },
256	  }
257	}

30	     * listener mounted records reach the backend as captured, so exported

2	
3	/**
4	 * Deployment-style redaction rule for the telemetry e2e: scrubs the fixture
5	 * credential from body strings, exactly as a real deployment would mount its
6	 * own rules on the `session-telemetry/record` waterfall.
7	 */
8	
9	const SECRET = /sk-e2efixture[0-9]+/g
10	const PLACEHOLDER = '[E2E-REDACTED]'
11	
12	function scrub(value: unknown): unknown {
13	  if (typeof value === 'string') return value.replace(SECRET, PLACEHOLDER)
14	  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(scrub)
15	  if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') {
16	    return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).map(([key, entry]) => [key, scrub(entry)]))
17	  }
18	  return value
19	}
20	
21	export const name = 'telemetry-redact-rule'
22	
23	/** Mount the fixture scrub rule onto the redact waterfall. */
24	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
25	  ctx.on('session-telemetry/record', (_record, next) => {
26	    const record = next()
27	    return { ...record, body: scrub(record.body) }
28	  })
29	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

1	# Agent Note: Attributable decisions and pinned data-use terms
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Two of the Village's governance promises have no producer in the log. The [Village note](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md) states that five transitions — spec freeze, relaxation of a security or compliance check, review acceptance, release, and training-data release — never complete without a `signoff/recorded` naming the principal and the artefact hash, and that every client-district session carries `dataUse/terms` from creation; the [four-goal note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) names the same two records `SignoffRecord` and `DataUseTerms`, puts them in blocking rollout item 3 beside `decidedBy` with an argument digest on approvals, and hangs the "Attributed human signer" roster row on them. Nothing writes any of the three today. `dsh-program` gates `requireSignoff` on a caller-supplied `spec.signoff` field its own README calls an assertion rather than a proof, the [program-ledger note](2026-09-06-program-ledger.md) defers the real record to this rollout, and the approval seam's `approval/decided` records an outcome with no principal and no statement of what was decided on. A client auditor reading a session log can therefore see that a program released, but not who released it, on what artefact, with what in view; and no export can tell an evaluation-only transcript from one a training run may consume.
10	
11	## Proposal
12	
13	Two plugins in a new `packages/governance/` group, plus two fields on the approval seam's existing audit pair. All three are log-first: nothing holds state a replay of the session log does not reproduce, and nothing reaches a model request.
14	
15	### `@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff`
16	
17	`ctx.signoffs.record(agent, { transition, principal, artefactSha256, evidence })` appends one `signoff/recorded` to the agent's session and returns the detached record. `transition` is the closed union `spec-freeze | relaxation | review-acceptance | release | training-data-release` — the five transitions of the Village note's Governance section. `principal` is `{ kind: 'human', id, displayName? }`, an identity string the deployment's identity provider supplies: the plugin records a principal, it never authenticates one. `artefactSha256` is a lowercase 64-hex digest of whatever the signer signed — a frozen spec, a certificate, a merged head, a dataset manifest. `evidence` is a bounded list of `{ kind, ref }` pointers to what the signer had in view, bounded by `Config.maxEvidence` and `Config.maxEvidenceRefChars` so one record cannot grow a session log without limit. `latest(agent, transition)` folds the session's own log for the newest record of one transition, and the pure `latestSignoff(events, transition)` folds any log a consumer already holds.
18	
19	The invariant companion rejects a malformed principal, a digest that is not lowercase 64-hex, an unknown transition, an evidence entry with an empty `kind` or `ref`, and a record whose `artefactSha256` differs from the digest the same session already recorded for the same transition. What it cannot check is everything outside the log: that the principal is the person named, that the digest addresses a real artefact, that the evidence refs resolve, or that the signer saw them.
20	
21	`dsh-program` switches both `requireSignoff` gates to that record. Opening a program reads `signoff/recorded { transition: 'spec-freeze' }` from the program session — recorded by the caller through `ctx.signoffs` before `start`, because the program session id is derived from the spec digest and is therefore addressable before the program exists — and releasing reads `signoff/recorded { transition: 'release' }` before `program/end { outcome: released }`. `spec.signoff` shrinks to `{ artefactSha256 }`: the frozen artefact digest each record must match, with the principal now coming from the record rather than from the caller.
22	
23	### `decidedBy` and `argumentsSha256` on approvals
24	
25	`ApprovalRequest` gains the decided call's `arguments`. The approval seam digests them once as a lowercase SHA-256 over their canonical JSON encoding and writes that digest to both `approval/asked` and `approval/decided`, so a decision states what it decided on rather than only which call id it belonged to. `approval/decided` also gains `decidedBy?: { kind: 'human' | 'policy', id }`. The `approval/request` waterfall's answer widens from an outcome to an outcome or `{ outcome, decidedBy }`, so an answerer that knows who decided attributes its own answer while every existing answerer keeps returning a bare outcome. The service attributes the one decision it makes itself: the deterministic `'never'` policy records `{ kind: 'policy', id: 'approval-policy:never' }`.
26	
27	The invariant companion rejects an `approval/decided` whose `argumentsSha256` differs from the digest its paired `approval/asked` recorded, including one carrying a digest its ask did not, and a `decidedBy` with an unknown `kind` or an empty `id`.
28	
29	### `@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use`
30	
31	`Config` states the deployment's default terms — `clientId`, `agreementId`, `purposes` (a non-empty subset of `delivery | training | evaluation`), `residency`, `retentionDays`, and `redactionProfile`, the `DataUseTerms` fields of the four-goal note. The plugin appends one `dataUse/terms` at every `agent/session-start` whose session does not already carry one, so a session created by any composition that mounts it is pinned from creation and a resumed session keeps the terms it was created under. `ctx.dataUse.pin(agent, terms)` records narrower terms for one session; a pin that widens `purposes` beyond what the session already carries is refused with `DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED` rather than appended, because widening after the fact would let a delivery-only session become a training corpus. `termsOf(events)` is the exported fold consumers read. The invariant companion rejects a second `dataUse/terms` that widens `purposes`.
32	
33	## Alternatives considered
34	
35	**One governance plugin holding both records.** Rejected: the two have different lifetimes and different consumers — a signoff is one attributed transition read by the program ledger and the release path, while data-use terms are a per-session pin read by the exporter and the curator — and a composition that needs terms without signatures is the ordinary client district.
36	
37	**Authenticating the principal.** Rejected as out of scope and out of place: the harness has no identity provider (`dsh-anonymous-user-id` is deliberately anonymous), and a plugin that verified a signature would need a key store, a revocation path, and a clock. The record states who the deployment says signed; making that binding is the identity provider's job and the deployment's.
38	
39	**Keeping the caller-supplied `spec.signoff` as the program's proof.** Rejected: it is the assertion the program README already flags, it carries a principal nothing can attribute, and it is invisible to the invariant companions and to every reader of the session log.
40	
41	**Putting the arguments themselves on `approval/asked`.** Rejected: the ask deliberately carries a `callId` rather than duplicating a tool call the log already holds, and a full argument copy would put secrets a redaction profile has not seen into a second place. A digest states what was decided on without restating it.
42	
43	**Deriving `decidedBy` inside the service from the answerer's registration.** Rejected: the registering plugin is not the principal — a UI answerer forwards a person's click and a machine answerer forwards a rule — so only the answerer can say which of the two decided.
44	
45	**Enforcing data-use terms rather than recording them.** Rejected for this slice: the exporter's refusal to emit a `training`-ineligible session is the enforcement, and it belongs with the exporter's redaction profile, which is not in this slice.
46	
47	## Acceptance criteria
48	
49	- A `signoff/recorded` names its transition, principal, artefact digest, and evidence, and `latest` folds the newest record of one transition from the log; the companion rejects a malformed principal, a non-hex digest, an unknown transition, and a second record of one transition under a different artefact digest, each with a failing fixture.
50	- `dsh-program` with `requireSignoff: true` refuses `start` without a `spec-freeze` record on the program session and refuses release without a `release` one, each with `PROGRAM_SIGNOFF_REQUIRED`, and refuses a record whose artefact digest is not the spec's.
51	- Every `approval/decided` carries the digest of the arguments its `approval/asked` recorded, the `'never'` policy attributes itself as `policy`, and the companion rejects a decision whose digest differs from its ask's.
52	- A session created under a composition holding `dsh-data-use` carries `dataUse/terms` before its first turn, a pin narrowing `purposes` is recorded, and a pin widening them is refused and appends nothing.
53	- A Loader-booted e2e over one `cordis.yml` composing both plugins, the approval seam, a mock route, persistence, and the checkpoint policy shows all four facts in the durable log.
54	
55	## Rollout
56	
57	1. This slice: `dsh-signoff`, `dsh-data-use`, `decidedBy` and `argumentsSha256` on the approval pair, the program gate switch, and the governance e2e.
58	2. The exporter integration: `dataUse/terms` decides which sessions a trajectory or facts export may emit, beside the held-out and district withholding it already applies, and the redaction profile the terms name becomes the export's own.
59	3. The remaining `SignoffRecord` fields of the four-goal note — `role`, `method`, and `scope` — once a stage vocabulary and an identity provider exist to fill them.
60	4. Attributing answerers: a UI or ACP answerer that carries the deciding person's identity records `kind: 'human'`.
61	
62	## Risks
63	
64	- **A record is only as good as its principal.** Nothing authenticates the id, so a deployment whose identity provider is a configuration string has an audit trail that names a role rather than a person; the companion cannot tell the difference and the README says so.
65	- **Terms pinned at creation, enforced nowhere yet.** Until the exporter reads them, `dataUse/terms` is a durable claim rather than a barrier, and a composition that omits `dsh-data-use` produces sessions with no terms at all.
66	- **`purposes` is the only monotone field.** Residency, retention, and the redaction profile can be re-pinned freely; only widening `purposes` is refused, because it is the field whose widening turns a delivery transcript into training data.
67	- **Two writers on one session.** As with `budget/caps`, nothing states which orchestrator owns a session's terms or signatures; the companions bound what a second writer can do, they do not decide who may write.
68
